Among non-MPR patients with evaluable Texp data, 32 of 64 (50.0%) had high Texp levels, defined by the median non-MPR cutoff for Texp.in.Tex.relevant*10 (>= 8.052753644). Using all non-MPR patients as the denominator, this is 32 of 70 (45.7%) because 6 non-MPR patients lacked Texp values.

These high-Texp non-MPR patients had favorable recurrence-free survival: 4/32 had recurrence events, Kaplan-Meier RFS was 90.2% at 12 months and 86.4% at 24 months, and median RFS was not reached. Compared with low-Texp non-MPR patients, high Texp was strongly associated with better RFS (log-rank p = 0.000391; Cox HR = 0.174, 95% CI 0.0585-0.519, p = 0.00171). Their RFS was not detectably worse than MPR/pCR responders (24-month RFS 86.4% vs 91.2%; log-rank p = 0.501; Cox HR = 1.58, 95% CI 0.445-5.59, p = 0.480), supporting a responder-like favorable RFS subgroup despite non-MPR status.
